disease_label_per_paper: Persistent Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia with evolving beta-lactam and carbapenem resistance during therapy
presentation_summary: 68-year-old man with follicular lymphoma treated with chemotherapy had a prolonged recent hospitalization complicated by febrile neutropenia, renal failure requiring hemodialysis, right leg cellulitis, and C. difficile colitis.

Two weeks after discharge he re-presented with recurrent right leg cellulitis, increased shortness of breath, loose stool, hypotension 80/40 mmHg, heart rate 129/min, oxygen saturation 75% on room air, and high Tmax on ICU day 1.

Admission blood cultures later grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa; serial cultures showed persistent bacteremia with progressive resistance to cefepime, piperacillin-tazobactam, meropenem, ceftazidime-avibactam, and ceftolozane-tazobactam.
He deteriorated with recurrent hypotension, respiratory failure, altered mental status, worsening renal failure, and died after transition to comfort measures.

risk_context.source_text_value: follicular lymphoma with bone marrow involvement treated with R-EPOCH/R-CHOP and bendamustine/rituximab
prolonged hospital course complicated by febrile neutropenia
3-month hospitalization with aztreonam, cefepime, anidulafungin, vancomycin, metronidazole, and other exposures
recurrence of right lower extremity cellulitis with erythema and induration extending to groin and left medial thigh

observations.source_text_value: medical ICU admission with Tmax 103.0 F
oxygen saturation of 75% in room air
6-month history of worsening fatigue, anorexia, and weight loss
right upper leg erythema and induration with extension to the groin and left medial thigh
hematologic malignancy, recent febrile neutropenia, prolonged hospitalization, broad antibiotic exposure, renal failure/hemodialysis context, cellulitis, shock
prolonged healthcare and broad antibiotic exposure before recurrent bacteremia
medical ICU admission with norepinephrine for hypotension

lab_trajectories.conversion_note: table reports WBC in cells/mm3 units but values are x10^3/microL-equivalent

clinical_course.source_text_value: Admission to the medical ICU, being started on norepinephrine for hypotension
Day 1 blood cultures grew P. aeruginosa
Blood culture from Day 5 resistant to cefepime
Intubated for decreased respiratory rate and apnea, hypotension (75/50), altered mental status
Blood culture from Day 10 grew P. aeruginosa resistant to meropenem; E-test showed resistance to ceftazidime-avibactam and ceftolozane-tazobactam
Reintubated for respiratory distress; hypotension despite fluids; patient on three vasopressors; repeat blood cultures drawn

microbiology.source_text_value: Blood cultures from the day of admission grew P. aeruginosa
Blood cultures persistently grew P. aeruginosa
subsequent resistance to all cephalosporins and penicillins by Day 5 and resistance to meropenem by Day 10; E-test showed resistance to ceftazidime-avibactam and ceftolozane-tazobactam
CTX-M, KPC, NDM, VIM, IMP, and OXA gene were not detected

imaging.source_text_value: Noncontrast CT scan of abdomen and pelvis showed bilateral pleural effusion, moderate ascites, generalized anasarca, no abscess
Transthoracic echo showed possible valvular vegetations; transesophageal echocardiogram did not reveal vegetations

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: persistent P. aeruginosa bacteremia resistant to ceftazidime-avibactam and ceftolozane-tazobactam
BC-GN assay did not detect CTX-M, KPC, NDM, VIM, IMP, or OXA genes

actual_treatment.source_text_value: Empiric vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam were started
Meropenem 1 g IV every 8 hours + tobramycin

outcome.source_text_value: Family decided to change code status to comfort measures only; he was extubated and expired

quality_warnings: Resistance phenotype and mechanism are confirmatory/treatment-context, not disease-name qualifiers.
The presentation preserves lymphoma, chemotherapy, prior neutropenia, renal failure, skin source context, and shock; these are risk/context axes and should not be hard-coded into the disease leaf.
